title: Stabilize tool selection precedence and stream-safe message framing for OpenAI compatibility
author: Jamal Ortega
description: Background: Customers integrating the OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling surface observed nondeterministic tool selection when multiple candidates matched a schema and intermittent corruption of framed streaming messages during rapid tool handoffs. This PR stabilizes selection precedence semantics and introduces a stream-safe framing coordinator to prevent partial-message leakage during tool invocation fallbacks. Motivation: Reduce customer-visible variance in tool_choice outcomes (affecting telemetry and deterministic evals) and stop streaming clients from receiving malformed chunks when we switch to a fallback tool mid-stream. Design summary: 1) Selection precedence: introduce an explicit, layered precedence model evaluated deterministically: exact signature match > schema-subset match > proto-compatible aliasing > fuzzy name match. The resolver now emits a deterministic tie-break key (deterministic hash of normalized signature+schema path) which is used to choose among candidates. 2) Message framing coordinator: add a stream_coordinator that tracks outstanding tool frame boundaries, drains partial frames before switching, and inserts clear boundary markers ("<|tool-start|>","<|tool-end|>") when processing OpenAI-compatible deltas. These markers are stripped by downstream SDKs but are preserved in server-side telemetry to aid debugging. 3) Backpressure and retry: when a fallback is required mid-stream, the coordinator initiates a short (configurable) drain window (default 50ms) to allow in-flight fragments to complete. If fragments do not arrive, coordinator emits a soft-fill token to close the last frame and starts the fallback tool's frame. 4) Compatibility: the change is additive for clients that do not rely on exact chunk contents; for strict byte-level consumers we provide a config flag to disable boundary markers and keep previous behavior. Checklist: - [x] Define deterministic precedence algorithm and deterministic tie-break key - [x] Implement resolver changes and unit tests - [x] Implement stream_coordinator and message markers - [x] Add integration tests for mid-stream fallback scenarios - [x] Update telemetry to record candidate list and selected strategy - [x] End-to-end testing against openai-compat SDK harness - [x] Docs note + migration guidance (see release_notes) Commit summary: 5 commits, largest changes are resolver rewrite and new framing coordinator with tests. CI: flakes on initial run (integration timeout in qemu build); re-ran and all checks passed (unit, linters, e2e). Observability: telemetry now emits tool_choice.candidate_count, tool_choice.selected_key, framing.drain_ms, and framing.boundary_inserted boolean. Files changed (high-level): - pkg/openai_compat/tool_resolver.go: replace ad-hoc matching with layered precedence and deterministic hash key; add extensive unit tests and mocks. - pkg/stream/framing/stream_coordinator.go: new coordinator implementing drain windows and fallback-safe switching. - pkg/stream/framing/message_marker.go: marker insertion/removal logic; feature flag gate. - pkg/api/handlers/tool_invoke_handler.go: integrate coordinator into invoke flow; ensure responses to streaming clients include marker sanitization unless opt-in. - pkg/telemetry/tool_choice_events.go: emit structured events for candidates and selected strategy. - tests/integration/toolcall_streaming_test.go: new scenarios for mid-stream tool switch, partial fragment arrival, and marker-preservation assertions. Migration notes: By default behavior is backward-compatible. Teams with custom byte-level parsers should either opt-in to the legacy no-marker mode by setting OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT_CHUNKS=true or update their SDKs to strip markers; we recommend updating since markers aid debugging. Release notes: "Stabilized OpenAI-compatible tool selection precedence and added stream-safe framing to prevent partial-fragment leakage during mid-stream tool fallbacks. Adds telemetry for tool_choice decisions." Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag openai_compat.stream_safe_framing and enabled for canary clusters for 48 hours before global rollout. Impact and risk: Medium; main risk is clients that perform exact-contents matching on stream chunks. We validated with canary tests and no regressions in latency beyond a median +2ms framing overhead. Support runbook: included in linked_linear ENG-2137; quick mitigation is to toggle OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT_CHUNKS to revert to legacy framing if a customer reports issues.
commit_summary: 5 commits: resolver: deterministic precedence; framing: new coordinator & markers; handler: integrate coordinator; telemetry: emit tool_choice events; tests: add integration scenarios
review_thread: Hannah Li (reviewer): Can we avoid adding markers by default? Concern about breaking some older SDKs. Author reply: We gate markers behind a feature flag and provide a strict-chunks env var for legacy behavior.
Priya Raman (reviewer): The deterministic hash depends on schema ordering—make sure we canonicalize. Author reply: Resolver now canonicalizes field order and normalizes type aliases before hashing.
Eric Novak (reviewer): Need benchmark of extra latency. Author reply: Added microbench and canary results; median +2ms overhead, p95 unchanged.
tests: Unit tests added for precedence, hashing, and markers (pkg/openai_compat/*). Integration test validates mid-stream fallback and marker stripping. E2E run against compat harness passed after CI rerun. Local perf benchmark included in pr artifacts.
release_notes: Stabilized OpenAI-compatible tool selection precedence; added stream-safe framing and boundary markers for tool handoffs. Default behavior remains backward-compatible; opt-out via OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT_CHUNKS.
files_changed_snippets: pkg/openai_compat/tool_resolver.go - core precedence switch and deterministic_key() function added
pkg/stream/framing/stream_coordinator.go - new drain window logic and fallback entrypoint
pkg/stream/framing/message_marker.go - marker constants and sanitizer pipeline
security_review: No PII changes. Security reviewed—no new data exfiltration paths introduced. Markers are internal and sanitized for public logs.
notes_for_release: Enable openai_compat.stream_safe_framing on canary for 48h; monitor tool_choice.candidate_count and framing.boundary_inserted metrics. Document SDK changes in compat guide.
